questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of the Adapter Pattern?

options.text: To allow incompatible interfaces to work together
To add responsibilities to objects dynamically
To define a one-to-many dependency between objects
To define a family of algorithms and make them interchangeable

questions.explanation: The correct answer is To allow incompatible interfaces to work together.

questions.stem: Explain how the Strategy Pattern can improve code maintainability and flexibility in a sorting application.
markingGuide: Discusses separation of algorithm from client code
Mentions ease of adding new algorithms
questions.explanation: The Strategy Pattern allows sorting algorithms to be encapsulated, making them interchangeable. This separation means client code does not need to change when a new sorting algorithm is added, improving maintainability and flexibility.

questions.stem: Discuss the trade-offs between using an Adapter and a Decorator in terms of system design.
markingGuide: Describes the purpose of the Adapter Pattern
Describes the purpose of the Decorator Pattern
Compares how each pattern affects system flexibility
questions.explanation: The Adapter Pattern is used to make incompatible interfaces work together, while the Decorator Pattern adds new functionality. Adapters can increase system flexibility by allowing integration with legacy systems, whereas Decorators can increase flexibility by allowing dynamic behavior changes. However, both patterns can add complexity to the system.
